Mireille Fontaine — CV bullets (Backend & Data Infrastructure)

Anchorwell Payments — Staff Backend Engineer (Jul 2023 – Present)
- Own the settlement reconciliation service that closes each business day's payment batches across three currencies, in production and under daily deadline pressure.
- Rebuilt the reconciliation pipeline from scratch after a 2023 data-loss incident during a database migration; it has processed every batch since without a repeat incident.
- Led migration of the payments ledger from a self-hosted Postgres cluster to a managed, multi-region database service.
- Built and maintained the fraud-signal ingestion path that feeds the risk team's models — responsible for the data plumbing upstream of a modelling team, though not for the models themselves.
- Introduced a canary deployment process for the payments API, giving the team a staged path to production for risky changes.
- Participate in the org-wide incident response rotation for payment-critical services.

Anchorwell Payments — Senior Backend Engineer (Feb 2021 – Jul 2023)
- Built the idempotency-key service used by the checkout team to prevent duplicate charges.
- Re-architected the payment authorization path to reduce peak-hour checkout latency.
- Served as on-call primary for the payments service for six consecutive quarters, debugging production failures back to root cause under live traffic.
- Wrote the internal runbook for PCI-DSS scope reduction that the security team adopted (engineering work; not a formal compliance-audit role).
- Mentored two mid-level engineers joining the payments team — informal mentoring, with no formal management, hiring or budget authority.

Harborline Payments — Backend Engineer (Mar 2018 – Feb 2021)
- Investigated and fixed a currency-conversion rounding error that had gone unnoticed for several months, tracing a silent data-correctness bug to its source.
- Migrated batch settlement jobs from ad hoc cron scripts to an Airflow-based pipeline.
- Implemented retry and backoff logic for failed card-network calls against unreliable external systems.
- Built the merchant onboarding API alongside the platform team; contributed test coverage for the refund processing service.
- Presented the settlement pipeline redesign at the company's internal quarterly engineering demo.

Voss Analytics — Software Engineer (Aug 2015 – Feb 2018)
- Built nightly ETL jobs loading client usage data into a reporting warehouse.
- Wrote the first version of the internal API behind the analytics dashboard, and performance-tuned slow SQL reports for the customer success team.
- Helped set up the team's first CI pipeline using Jenkins.

Kestrel Digital — Junior Developer (Jul 2014 – Jul 2015)
- Built internal Python tooling for the operations team; fixed bugs on the client-facing booking site and documented the internal deployment process.

Skills
- Production languages: Go, Python, Java. Postgres and managed multi-region databases, Airflow, Jenkins, canary deployments, managed queue services.

Scope note (offered up front)
- My background is backend and data infrastructure in payments and analytics. I have not worked on machine learning or computer-vision systems, have not deployed to edge or embedded hardware, have no C++ or PyTorch experience, and have no robotics-industry experience, publications or patents. What I bring to a Perception team is production data-pipeline ownership, deployment safety practice, and root-cause debugging of live systems — the infrastructure side of the role, not the modelling side.

job.raw_text:
Machine Learning Engineer - Perception
Solstice Vision Labs - Onsite (Toronto) preferred, remote considered for senior candidates

About us

Solstice Vision Labs builds computer vision systems for autonomous inspection robots
used in warehouses and light manufacturing. Our perception stack has to work on
real, messy hardware in the field, not just in a notebook.

The role

We're looking for a Machine Learning Engineer to join our Perception team. You'll work
across the full lifecycle of our vision models: collecting and labeling data, training,
and getting models running reliably on the robot's onboard compute. This is a
production-focused role - we care more about a model that runs correctly on the robot
than one that looks good on a benchmark.

Responsibilities

- Build and improve computer vision models used in production on our robots
- Work with our data annotation pipeline to decide what gets labeled next
- Get models running within the memory and latency limits of embedded hardware
- Debug production failures back to a root cause, whether that's data, model, or camera
- Collaborate with hardware engineers on camera placement and calibration

What you'll need

- Hands-on experience building and deploying computer vision models to a production
  system, not only research or coursework
- Strong Python skills; C++ experience is a plus for the embedded-deployment side
- Experience with PyTorch or a comparable deep learning framework
- Experience working with a data annotation or labeling pipeline
- Comfortable working within hardware constraints such as edge or embedded deployment

Nice to have

- Peer-reviewed publications or patents related to computer vision or robotics
- Experience mentoring junior scientists or engineers
- Prior robotics industry experience
- Experience helping set technical research direction for a team, not just executing it
- Familiarity with backend or cloud infrastructure, for teams that also ship a
  cloud-connected fleet dashboard

Compensation & benefits

Salary band posted per local pay transparency requirements, equity, health benefits,
and relocation assistance for candidates moving to Toronto. Solstice Vision Labs is
an equal opportunity employer.
